proposals.before: The Kuaiji dian lu says Sun Ce had credited Cao Teng of Wei for service; when Teng gave offense and was condemned to death, the gentry were terrified and could see no way out.
proposals.after: The Kuaiji dian lu says Sun Ce's merit clerk Wei Teng gave offense and was condemned to death; the gentry were terrified and could see no way out.
proposals.reason: Chinese 策功曹魏騰 is "Ce's merit clerk Wei Teng," not "Cao Teng of Wei"; 功曹 is the office and 魏騰 the personal name.

proposals.before: The Kuaiji dian lu states: Ce had credited Cao Teng of Wei for merit; because he gave offense he was reprimanded and was about to be executed; scholar-officials were anxious and fearful, with no plan to offer.
proposals.after: The Kuaiji dian lu states: Ce's merit clerk Wei Teng, because he gave offense, was reprimanded and was about to be executed; scholar-officials were anxious and fearful, with no plan to offer.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 功曹魏騰 as Cao Teng of Wei instead of merit clerk Wei Teng.

proposals.before: Cao Teng has served you faithfully with honest counsel. Kill him today and tomorrow every man will turn against you.
proposals.after: Merit clerk Wei has served you faithfully with honest counsel. Kill him today and tomorrow every man will turn against you.
proposals.reason: 魏功曹 refers to Wei the merit clerk (Wei Teng), not Cao Teng.

proposals.before: Sun Ce was shaken and released Cao Teng at once.
proposals.after: Sun Ce was shaken and released Wei Teng at once.
proposals.reason: Matches the Chinese personal name 騰 / 魏騰, correcting the earlier Cao Teng misidentification.

proposals.before: In the eighth year of the reign Wu Jing died at court; his son Wu Fen took command, became Marquis of Xinting, and predeceased his father.
proposals.after: In the eighth year Wu Jing died at court; his son Wu Fen was given troops as a general, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinting, and died.
proposals.reason: Chinese 卒 after Fen's appointments does not say he died before his father; Jing has already died in the same sentence.

proposals.before: When Wu Jing came back, Sun Quan reasoned that Wu Jing had once served in
proposals.after: When Wu Jing came back, because Jing had previously served in
proposals.reason: Continuation in s0061 attributes the judgment to Ce (策嫌其太重), not Sun Quan; the idiomatic invents Sun Quan.

proposals.before: He; favor was second to the Bu clan.
proposals.after: He; favor was second to Lady Bu.
proposals.reason: 步氏 here is the individuated Lady Bu, not an undifferentiated Bu clan collective.

proposals.before: When Lady Bu died and Sun He became heir, Sun Quan meant to make this Lady Wang empress; Princess Quan (Sun Luban), who had always detested her, whispered slander until the match collapsed.
proposals.after: When Lady Bu died and Sun He became heir, Sun Quan meant to make this Lady Wang empress; but Princess Quan (Sun Luban), who had always detested her, gradually whispered slander against her.
proposals.reason: Chinese 稍稍譖毀 states gradual slander only; 'until the match collapsed' invents an outcome not in this unit.

proposals.before: Lady Wang's face lit with ill-concealed hope; Sun Quan saw it, raged at her disloyalty, and she died of grief and fear.
proposals.after: She showed a joyful expression; Sun Quan therefore deeply blamed and angered her, and she died of grief.
proposals.reason: Source has 言有喜色 and 深責怒 / 以憂死; 'ill-concealed hope', 'disloyalty', and 'fear' are interpretive additions.

proposals.before: The Wang clan had no posterity; he enfeoffed her uterine younger brother Wen Yong as precinct marquis.
proposals.after: The Wang clan had no posterity; he enfeoffed her uterine younger brother Wang Wenyong as precinct marquis.
proposals.reason: 文雍 is the given name; English should retain the Wang surname already established for this lady's clan.

proposals.before: Broad, tolerant, kind, and gracious—you had virtuous and excellent virtue.
proposals.after: Broad, tolerant, kind, and gracious—you had the virtue of refined excellence.
proposals.reason: 淑懿之德 is one virtue-phrase; 'virtuous and excellent virtue' is redundant and obscures the epithet.

proposals.before: Once Lady Pan and Sun Liang rose, Princess Quan—feuding with Sun He's mother—talked Sun Quan into marrying Quan Shang's daughter to young Liang, making Liang heir.
proposals.after: Once Lady Pan and her son had favor, Princess Quan—feuding with Sun He's mother—talked Sun Quan into marrying Quan Shang's daughter to young Liang, making Liang heir.
proposals.reason: Chinese 潘夫人母子有寵 is mother-and-son favor; the idiomatic rendering drops 母子.

proposals.before: When Wei general Zhuge Dan came over from Shouchun, Quan Yi, Quan Duan, Quan Yi, Quan Yi, and the rest of that clan used the turmoil to defect to Wei.
proposals.after: When Wei general Zhuge Dan came over from Shouchun, Quan Yi (全懌), Quan Duan, Quan Yi (全禕), Quan Yi (全儀), and others used the turmoil to defect to Wei.
proposals.reason: Distinct given names 懌, 禕, and 儀 are collapsed to identical English Quan Yi.

proposals.before: Your servant Songzhi considers that Xiu married his nephew's daughter, the case being the same as Emperor Hui of Han.
proposals.after: Your servant Songzhi considers that Xiu married his niece (his sister's daughter), the case being the same as Emperor Hui of Han.
proposals.reason: 甥 here is the sister's child (niece); nephew's daughter misstates the kinship.

proposals.before: Princess Quan, terrified, said, "I truly knew nothing—it all came from Zhu Ju's sons Xiong and Sun."
proposals.after: Princess Quan, terrified, said, "I truly knew nothing—it all came from Zhu Ju's sons Xiong and Sun (損)."
proposals.reason: 損 romanized as Sun is easily confused with the imperial surname Sun.

proposals.before: Sun's wife was Jun's younger sister; Sun Chen grew ever more jealous of Liang, then deposed Liang and established Xiu.
proposals.after: Sun's (損's) wife was Jun's younger sister; Sun Chen grew ever more jealous of Liang, then deposed Liang and established Xiu.
proposals.reason: Opening Sun's wife reads as the imperial surname rather than Zhu Sun (損).

proposals.before: As Lady Teng's favor waned Sun Hao grew angry, while his mother Lady He always sided against her.
proposals.after: As Lady Teng's favor waned Sun Hao grew angry, while his mother Lady He always sided with her.
proposals.reason: Chinese 左右之 here means assist/support Lady Teng; the next sentence shows she was not deposed with Lady He's backing, so 'against' reverses the sense.

proposals.before: The Shi jing states: "Model yourself on your few wife, reaching to your brothers, thereby to regulate family and state."
proposals.after: The Shi jing states: "Be a pattern to your consort, reaching to your brothers, thereby to regulate family and state."
proposals.reason: 寡妻 means the ruler's consort, not a 'few wife'; the mistranslation obscures the appraisal's point.

proposals.before: The Shi jing states: "Model yourself on your few wife, reaching to your brothers, thereby to regulate family and state."
proposals.after: The Shi jing states: "Be a pattern to your consort, reaching to your brothers, thereby to regulate family and state."
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 寡妻 is 'consort', not 'few wife'.

proposals.before: Sun Xiu's general amnesty let him return; Teng Mu was named a Gentlemen of the Five Offices.
proposals.after: Sun Xiu's general amnesty let him return; Teng Mu was named a Gentleman of the Five Offices.
proposals.reason: 五官中郎 is singular; 'Gentlemen' is a grammatical error.

decisions.reason: 策功曹魏騰 is Sun Ce's merit clerk Wei Teng; the before text misreads 魏騰 as Cao Teng of Wei.
Same misparse: 功曹 is the office and 魏騰 the personal name, not Cao Teng of Wei.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 策功曹魏騰，以迕意見譴，將殺之

decisions.reason: 魏功曹 is Wei the merit clerk (Wei Teng), continuing s0160; Cao Teng is a false identity.
遽釋騰 releases Teng (魏騰); Cao Teng is unsupported.
After 景卒宮, Fen is given troops, enfeoffed, then 卒; the Chinese does not say he predeceased his already-dead father.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 八年，景卒宮，子奮授兵為將，封新亭侯，卒

decisions.reason: 以景前在 continues into s0061 where 策嫌其太重; inventing Sun Quan as the reasoner is unsupported.
In this consort biography 步氏 is Lady Bu, as confirmed by the next unit 步氏薨後, not a clan collective.
稍稍譖毀 reports only gradual slander; 'until the match collapsed' invents an outcome absent from this unit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 全公主素憎夫人，稍稍譖毀

decisions.after: She showed a joyful expression in speaking; Sun Quan therefore deeply reproached her in anger, and she died of grief.
decisions.reason: Removing invented 'hope', 'disloyalty', and 'fear' is needed, but the proposal also drops 言 and softens 深責怒; restore speaking and reproach-in-anger.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 言有喜色，由是權深責怒，以憂死

decisions.reason: The Chinese writes only 文雍; literal 'Wen Yong' is accurate enough, and adding the inferred surname is stylistic for this field.
淑懿之德 is a single virtue phrase; 'virtuous and excellent virtue' is redundant and obscures the epithet.
潘夫人母子有寵 is mother-and-son favor; 'Lady Pan and Sun Liang rose' drops 母子 and invents a different framing.

decisions.after: When Wei general Zhuge Dan came over from Shouchun, Quan Yì, Quan Duan, Quan Yī, Quan Yí, and others used the turmoil to defect to Wei.
decisions.reason: 全懌、全禕、全儀 are three distinct given names collapsed to identical 'Quan Yi'; full tone-marked pinyin distinguishes them cleanly without Chinese characters in the English field.
Context shows Lady Zhu is Xiu's sister's daughter; 甥 here is the niece, not a nephew's daughter.

decisions.after: Princess Quan, terrified, said, "I truly knew nothing—it all came from Zhu Ju's sons Xiong and Zhu Sun."
decisions.reason: 損 romanized alone as Sun is easily read as the imperial surname; restore the Zhu surname already used for his brother Xiong, without inserting Chinese characters.

decisions.after: Zhu Sun's wife was Jun's younger sister; Sun Chen grew ever more jealous of Liang, then deposed Liang and established Xiu.
decisions.reason: Opening 'Sun's wife' can be misread as the imperial surname; name him Zhu Sun in English only, matching the adjacent idiomatic wording.
左右之 means Lady He assisted/supported Lady Teng; 'sided against' reverses the sense confirmed by 故得不廢.
刑於寡妻 means set a pattern for one's consort; 'few wife' mistranslates 寡妻 and obscures the appraisal.
Same Shijing line: 寡妻 is consort, not 'few wife'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 刑於寡妻，至於兄弟，以御於家邦

decisions.reason: 五官中郎 is a singular office; 'Gentlemen' is a grammatical number error.
